title: These Headphones Twist Into a Bluetooth Speaker in Seconds. If Only They Sounded Better
gist: WIRED gives the $249 TDM Neo, CES 2026 on-ear headphones that twist into a 10-watt Bluetooth speaker, a 5/10. Reviewer Chris Haslam praises the magnetic twist mechanism and the battery life of more than 200 hours, but finds the sound boxed in, the fit tight and the speaker thin. He says buying the Soundcore Space One Pro and JBL Flip 7 separately costs about the same and works better.

insights.claim: The TDM Neo, unveiled at CES 2026, are on-ear headphones whose ear cups rotate and snap together magnetically to become a Bluetooth speaker. The headphone drivers switch off and outward-facing speakers take over. WIRED found the mechanism never popped open by accident.
insights.speaker: Chris Haslam
insights.so_what: Real form-factor innovation in consumer audio is rare, and in this case it raised money on Kickstarter and won awards.
insights.quote: Once connected, the headphone drivers disable, and the outward-facing Bluetooth speakers kick in.

insights.claim: The TDM Neo has four 40-mm drivers, two for the headphones and two 5-watt speakers (10 W total). Rated battery life is more than 200 hours in headphone mode and 16 hours in speaker mode, and a five-minute charge adds eight hours.
insights.speaker: Chris Haslam
insights.so_what: The battery figures are well above typical headphones, a spec that rivals may have to match.

insights.claim: WIRED argues that most portable audio products now focus on incremental updates and new colorways rather than real technical innovation. That makes a novel design like the TDM Neo stand out with the media and crowdfunding backers.
insights.speaker: Chris Haslam
insights.so_what: Incumbent audio brands look stagnant on product, which leaves an opening for startups with new form factors.
insights.quote: Most designs seem to revolve around incremental updates and new colorways rather than genuine technical innovation.
insights.locator: Given the current state of the portable audio industry

insights.claim: The TDM Neo has no active noise cancellation and relies on a tight on-ear fit for passive isolation. That is unusual now that Sony, Bose, Apple and Nothing focus on over-ear ANC designs.
insights.speaker: Chris Haslam
insights.so_what: Leaving out ANC puts the product outside where the mainstream premium headphone market is heading.

insights.claim: At 11.9 ounces, the TDM Neo is 3 ounces (34%) heavier than the Sony WH-1000XM6, 1.9 ounces heavier than the Soundcore Space One Pro and 4.25 ounces heavier than the Beats Solo 4.
insights.speaker: Chris Haslam
insights.so_what: Putting two products in one adds weight and costs comfort.
insights.locator: At 11.9-ounces, the Neo are also heavy

insights.claim: In speaker mode, the TDM Neo only keeps pace with the 4.5-watt $55 JBL Go 5 despite having twice the power and drivers. It is far behind the $120 JBL Flip 7, which shows that wattage alone does not decide speaker quality in the age of DSP.
insights.speaker: Chris Haslam
insights.so_what: JBL's compact speakers set a high bar, and hybrid devices have trouble beating dedicated products on sound.
insights.quote: the difference between the two was like racing a speedboat and a paddleboard
insights.locator: There's enough volume for casual listening

insights.claim: The $200 Soundcore Space One Pro ANC headphones, often on sale for $130-140, plus the $150 JBL Flip 7 cost about the same as the $249 TDM Neo. WIRED says the pair delivers top-tier sound in both categories, so the Neo's main advantage is carrying and charging one device.
insights.speaker: Chris Haslam
insights.so_what: Novelty combo devices struggle on value against discounted single-purpose products from Anker's Soundcore and JBL.
insights.locator: Two for the Price of One?

insights.claim: WIRED rated the TDM Neo 5/10. It praised the design and battery but criticized the sound quality, the lack of ANC, the tight fit and the price compared with buying separate devices.
insights.speaker: Chris Haslam
insights.so_what: A middling review from a major outlet could slow retail sales after the Kickstarter launch.
insights.quote: I just wish I enjoyed listening to them as much as I enjoyed twisting them.
insights.locator: I admire what TDM has achieved.

insights.claim: WIRED's reviewer says the TDM Neo is a reminder that innovation should not depend only on adding AI features, new colorways or another smartphone app.
insights.speaker: Chris Haslam
insights.so_what: There is some reviewer fatigue with AI feature-stuffing in consumer electronics.
insights.quote: innovation doesn't—and shouldn’t—rely solely on stuffing in AI features, adding a fresh colorway, or creating another smartphone app
insights.locator: I admire what TDM has achieved.
